analysis.summary: France enter as overwhelming favorites after a commanding 3-1 win over Senegal on matchday 1, with Kylian Mbappe becoming France's all-time leading scorer and the attacking trident of Mbappe, Olise, and Barcola looking sharp. Iraq were beaten 4-1 by Norway in their opener, creating only 0.77 xG against a side weaker than France, and head coach Graham Arnold acknowledged this is their toughest assignment. This is the first-ever competitive meeting between these nations. France's superior squad depth, elite attackers, and Iraq's defensive frailty make a heavy France win the most likely outcome.
analysis.home_form: France won 4 of last 5 matches including World Cup opener: 3-1 vs Senegal (Mbappe 2, Barcola), 3-1 vs Northern Ireland (friendly), 3-1 vs Colombia (friendly), 2-1 vs Brazil (friendly), 1-2 loss to Ivory Coast (friendly with PSG players rested). Mbappe is France's all-time scorer with 58 goals. Olise provided assists and a hat-trick in pre-tournament warm-up. France lineup vs Senegal: 4-2-3-1 with Maignan; Kounde, Upamecano, Saliba, T.Hernandez; Tchouameni, Rabiot; Olise, Dembele, Doue; Mbappe. Expected changes vs Iraq: Barcola to start (scored as sub vs Senegal), Digne and Kone also tipped to come in.
analysis.away_form: Iraq lost 1-4 to Norway in their World Cup opener, creating just 0.77 xG (1 shot on target from 11 attempts). Aymen Hussein scored Iraq's sole goal (header, 39'). Iraq conceded twice before half-time and were overrun in the second half. During AFC qualifying, Iraq averaged only 0.77 goals conceded per game under Arnold, but Norway exposed them badly. Arnold's pragmatic 4-4-2 relies on defensive organization, but they were overwhelmed by Haaland and company. Iraq have been out of the World Cup since 1986. Zaid Tahseen picked up a yellow card vs Norway (86', caution only, no suspension). Arnold confirmed Ali Jassim is fit and expected to start.
analysis.h2h: France and Iraq have never previously met in a senior international fixture — this is their first-ever encounter.
injuries_news: France: No significant injuries or suspensions reported ahead of matchday 2. Deschamps expected to rotate with Barcola starting, Digne and Kone coming in. No yellow card accumulation concern after one game.

Iraq: Defender Ahmed Yahya missed the tournament with a hamstring injury (replaced by Ahmed Maknzi in squad). Goalkeeper Jalal Hassan also absent. Zaid Tahseen (yellow vs Norway) — no suspension risk yet. Ali Jassim confirmed fit by Arnold. Youssef Amyn had hamstring issues pre-tournament; status unconfirmed for this game.
key_factors: France's attacking depth is world-class: Mbappe, Olise, Barcola, and Dembele all in peak form, capable of cutting open Iraq's 4-4-2 block repeatedly.
Iraq conceded 4 goals to Norway (xGA 2.59) — their defensive structure was repeatedly broken by crosses and movement. France's wide attacking play is likely to be even more damaging.
Iraq's offensive output was minimal (0.77 xG vs Norway); France's defense (Saliba, Upamecano, Maignan) is significantly stronger than Norway's, reducing Iraq's scoring chances further.
Tournament context: France need a win to maintain top position alongside Norway; Iraq must score to stay alive. Arnold has pledged to attack, which may open space for French counters.
First-ever meeting between these sides — no head-to-head adjustment needed, France's class differential is the dominant factor.
Philadelphia heat and a long trip from Boston for Iraq (6 days since last match). France had the same 6-day gap.
